summary: Complete target-level pass for the module-patching layer: finite decorated action data, cofinal cutoffs, simultaneous extraction, a native presented patched module, continuous actions and specialization, free and balanced numerical patching, and Kisin’s rational criterion. Retains both integrated target identifiers. Imports coefficient, depth, finiteness and support ownership instead of re-planning them. Three precise supplier interfaces remain recorded; complete means the planning pass is finished, not proof closure or implementation.

nodes.title: Balanced modules
nodes.statement: For a Noetherian local commutative ring S with residue field k and a finite S-module M, put β₀=dim_k(M/m_S M), β₁=dim_k Tor₁^S(M,k), and defect=β₀−β₁ in ℤ. M is balanced iff defect≥0. Equivalently, it admits an exact presentation S^d → S^d → M → 0 for some d; for balanced M one may take d=β₀. The suggested native predicate uses existence of a square presentation, and its agreement with this source definition is a separate comparison target.
hypotheses: S Noetherian local; M finite; Tor is endowed with its genuine k-module structure.
proofSteps: Choose a minimal finite-free resolution; reduction modulo m_S has zero differentials, giving β_i equal to the ith free rank.
If β₁≤β₀, pad the relation map by zero columns to make it square. Conversely any square presentation bounds the minimal relation count by its generator count after minimalizing.
acceptance: Integer subtraction, not truncated natural subtraction.
The zero module is balanced; a regular local residue field of embedding dimension two is not.

nodes.title: Balanced modules and square presentations
nodes.statement: Under the preceding local Noetherian finite hypotheses, balance, β₁≤β₀, and existence of a square presentation are equivalent. There exists a square presentation with d=β₀ precisely when M is balanced. Square presentations may be nonminimal; they do not imply projective dimension ≤1 until injectivity of the first map is separately proved.
hypotheses: M may be zero; minimal resolutions need not terminate.
proofSteps: Use the first two ranks of a minimal resolution.
Cancel unit entries in any finite presentation over the local ring, leaving β₀ generators and at most β₀ relations.
Preserve the selected basis of the generator free module when padding the minimal relation map.
acceptance: S=k[ε]/(ε²), M=k is balanced although its minimal resolution is infinite.

nodes.title: Taylor–Wiles group rings as series quotients
nodes.statement: Let O be the integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p, π a uniformizer, q≥0 and N≥1. Set S=O[[z₁,…,z_q]], a=(z₁,…,z_q), a_N=((1+z_i)^(p^N)−1)_i. There is a continuous O-algebra equivalence S/a_N ≃ O[(ℤ/p^Nℤ)^q] sending 1+z_i to the ith standard group element. It identifies a with the group augmentation ideal, and the finite-level transition maps with the quotient maps for a_{N+1}⊂a_N. Consequently S is the completed group algebra in this abelian finite-rank case; no general noncommutative Iwasawa algebra is introduced.
hypotheses: O complete DVR with finite residue field of characteristic p; coefficient maps local; q=0 allowed.
proofSteps: The finite group ring is a finite free complete O-module; g_i−1 is topologically nilpotent since its reduction is nilpotent. Use R03.1 local series evaluation.

The relation quotient has finite special fibre, because f_i mod π=z_i^(p^N); R03.4 gives O-module finiteness. Its finite-module completeness makes the image of the polynomial group algebra closed and dense, hence surjective.
Construct the reverse map from the group generators 1+z_i, which are units of order dividing p^N; check both composites on O and z_i using continuous evaluation uniqueness.
acceptance: At q=0 both rings are O and a=0.
Do not identify the finite group ring with a finite ring before also reducing π.

sources.locator: §2.2, Proposition 2.3 and proof, PDF pp. 11–14
sources.match: Uses the finite group rings and their compatible power-series presentation, with augmentation explicitly identified.

nodes.title: Finite cofinal patching cutoffs
nodes.statement: In the group-ring setting, b_N=(π^N,a_N) are descending open ideals cofinal with the maximal-ideal powers of S and with intersection zero. If H≠0 is a finite R-module finite over O, R is CNL_O(k), and J=Ann_R H, then d_N=(π^N,J^N) are descending open cofinal ideals of R with π^N R⊂d_N⊂π^N R+J. Thus R/d_N and S/b_N are finite, and d_N acts on H through π^N. These cutoffs are one permissible choice, not part of the invariant definition of patching.
hypotheses: H≠0, so J⊂m_R; the zero-H case is treated separately in the balanced theorem.
proofSteps: R/J embeds in End_O H and is finite O by the existing faithful-module finiteness criterion; hence radical(π,J)=m_R.
Noetherianity implies that d_N contains a maximal-ideal power, while d_N⊂m_R^N.
The binomial coefficients in f_{i,N} tend to zero in every fixed low degree, so b_N eventually lies inside any fixed maximal-ideal power; π and the variable powers make each b_N open.
Use the pinned finite quotient criterion and completeness from R03.1.
acceptance: The maps R/d_N→End(H/π^N H) need not be injective.
Cofinality, rather than intersection zero alone for an arbitrary filtration, is part of the interface.

sources.locator: §2.2, Proposition 2.3 and proof, PDF pp. 11–14

nodes.title: Finite decorated patching data
nodes.statement: Fix finite O-algebras T=S/I and D=R/J, integers d,r≥0, an augmentation ideal a⊂S, a finite T-module target H₀ killed by a, and a CNL_O(k) action ring A. A datum consists of a based T-linear map P:T^r→T^d, X=coker P (or a specified equivalence with that native quotient), an O-algebra action ρ:A→End_T(X), a continuous local surjection φ:A→D, a surjection q:X→H₀ with ker q=aX, and equality q(ρ(a₀)x)=φ(a₀)·q(x) for every a₀∈A. The D-action on H₀ is fixed and compatible with its T-action. Equivalence preserves the actual action, φ, q and the chosen presentation maps; a module isomorphism alone is insufficient. The presentation is part of the decoration; arbitrary changes of bases are recorded explicitly when used.
hypotheses: All rings and modules carry the stated O-actions; T and D have finite cardinality.
The augmentation ideal action means its image in T; all actions commute.
proofSteps: Use native finite free coordinate modules, linear-map range quotient and endomorphism ring.
Express the augmentation comparison as the exact quotient map q, avoiding a new completed tensor carrier.
Define equivalence by a T-linear equivalence intertwining both ring actions, the fixed generator projection and q; relation matrices in fixed bases reduce literally.
acceptance: Equality of φ is mandatory even when X has a nonfaithful action.
A finite extra list of commuting comparison maps can be added as decorations; its size is fixed across levels.

nodes.title: Finiteness of decorated patching data
nodes.statement: At fixed finite quotients T,D,H₀ and fixed d,r, the set of equivalence classes of finite patch data is finite. In particular there are finitely many possible continuous A-actions, not just presentation matrices. For X generated by d elements, |X|≤|T|^d=K. The commutative image E of A in End_T(X) is a finite local quotient of A with |E|≤K^K (treat X=0 separately); the descending maximal-ideal powers of E stabilize only at zero by Nakayama, giving m_A^(K^K)X=0. Therefore every action factors through a fixed finite quotient A/m_A^(K^K). Add finitely many fixed finite comparison objects without losing finiteness.
hypotheses: A Noetherian local with finite residue field; fixed generator bound d; quotient T finite.
A action is O-linear and commutes with T; no faithfulness of X as A-module is assumed.
proofSteps: There are finitely many matrices T^r→T^d; choose the canonical cokernel for each.
Bound the size of End_T X by all set maps X→X. The image of the commutative local ring A is local and finite, so its maximal ideal is nilpotent with a uniform cardinality bound.
Use the pinned finite quotient criterion for A/m_A^e, and count homomorphisms between finite carriers, maps to H₀ and comparison maps.
φ factors through a fixed finite quotient as well; take the maximum cutoff required by action and target D.
acceptance: A generator bound for X alone is not used as a substitute for an A-action cutoff.

nodes.title: Compatible presentation towers
nodes.statement: For descending cofinal open ideals I_n⊂S and J_n⊂R, a compatible patch tower is a family of finite patch data over S/I_n and R/J_n with specified isomorphisms from reduction of level n+1 to level n. These intertwine presentations in fixed bases, both actions, φ_n and q_n. Their iterated composites define the native ℕᵒᵖ-indexed module functor; identity and composition are genuine equations. For an extracted tower, retain separately the two subsequence indices with their strict growth and original-level≥cutoff-level conditions. A tower is extra selected data; the input modules H_N are not assumed to have transition maps.
hypotheses: Fixed presentation sizes d,r; each finite-level augmentation target is H/L_n H with compatible L_n.
Cofinal ideals and all reduction isomorphisms are specified, not inferred from isomorphism classes.
proofSteps: Use the native category-theoretic inverse-system functor and actual reduction isomorphisms.
Compose the adjacent maps to supply all arrows; quotient coherence follows from their chosen definition.
Keep the subsequence witnesses separate from the abstract tower, so no false canonical choice is exposed.
acceptance: The tower includes explicit, action-preserving transition morphisms.

nodes.title: Simultaneous finite-data extraction
nodes.statement: Suppose for each m≥n≥1 one has a finite patch datum D_{m,n}, reduction to all smaller cutoffs is defined coherently, and the presentation sizes and finite decorations are fixed. Then there exist strictly increasing sequences m_i,n_i with m_i≥n_i, both unbounded, and chosen isomorphisms red_{n_i}(D_{m_{i+1},n_{i+1}})≃D_{m_i,n_i} preserving all decorations. Thus the chosen data form a compatible patch tower. No compatibility between the original arithmetic levels m is an input.
hypotheses: Finiteness of equivalence classes at each cutoff, proved including the action cutoff.
Arbitrarily large original levels supply a datum at every fixed cutoff.
proofSteps: At cutoff 1 select a class occurring for infinitely many original levels; repeat inside that infinite set at successive cutoffs.
Keep finite sets of concrete representatives and finite choices of isomorphisms at each finite prefix.

Use the pinned finite inverse-system section theorem on the nonempty finite extendible-prefix system; then choose original levels recursively from the retained infinite sets, larger than both their cutoff and the previous original level.
Recover explicit reduction maps and retain simultaneous comparisons.
acceptance: A tower of bare isomorphism classes without chosen action-preserving maps does not meet the conclusion.

nodes.title: The patched module from a limit presentation
nodes.statement: For a compatible tower of based presentations (S/I_n)^r → (S/I_n)^d → X_n → 0 over a complete Noetherian local ring S, lift every matrix coefficient along the cofinal quotient system to obtain P_∞:S^r→S^d. Define PatchedModule=(S^d)/range(P_∞) using the native module quotient. Equip it with its finite S-module structure and maximal-ideal topology. Its canonical reductions and comparison with the native inverse limit are established in the next target, so this is a single carrier rather than a second definition of inverse limit.
hypotheses: S complete Noetherian local with finite residue field; I_n descending open cofinal.
Fixed finite presentation sizes and fixed bases; genuine matrix compatibility.
proofSteps: Use completeness to lift each of the finitely many compatible entries; compare cofinal cutoffs with native ideal powers.
Use the coordinate linear map and its native range quotient.
Finite generation descends from the generator free module.
acceptance: Only P_∞ and the selected tower determine this carrier; there is no independence assertion for unrelated extractions.

nodes.title: Presentation and inverse-limit comparison
nodes.statement: For the preceding tower, the canonical map PatchedModule→lim X_n is an equivalence of S-modules and of their adic topological modules; PatchedModule/I_n PatchedModule≃X_n. The sequence S^r→S^d→PatchedModule→0 is exact at S^d and PatchedModule. Neither injectivity of the relation map nor general exactness of arbitrary inverse limits is asserted.
hypotheses: The fixed bases make the compatible matrix P_∞ literal.
Finite S-modules are complete for the maximal-ideal topology because S is complete Noetherian.
proofSteps: Right exactness of quotient/base change gives each reduction equivalence from the finite presentation.

Derive finite-module completeness: S is the compact limit of its finite maximal-ideal quotients; M is the continuous quotient of a finite free compact module, and the pinned Noetherian finite-module Hausdorff theorem makes its quotient topology Hausdorff. Thus M is compact and complete. Use the cofinal comparison to identify the canonical module with the limit of its reductions.

Alternatively lift the finite preimage fibres of P_∞ by the pinned finite-system section theorem. For completion exactness use the short exact sequence ker(S^d→M)→S^d→M, whose kernel is finite by Noetherianity.
Do not apply completion exactness to a presentation matrix assumed injective.
acceptance: The identity and uniformizer matrices give distinct cokernels; all quotient maps are generator-compatible.

sources.locator: §2.2, Proposition 2.3 and proof, PDF pp. 11–14

nodes.title: Continuous action on the patched module
nodes.statement: For a decorated compatible tower, construct the O-algebra action ρ_∞:A→End_S(PatchedModule) from the finite-level actions via the native limit comparison. Construct φ_∞:A→R from φ_n:A↠R/J_n. Both maps are continuous in the pointwise adic endomorphism topology and the maximal-ideal ring topologies. φ_∞ is surjective: for each r∈R the nonempty compact fibres above its finite reductions have the finite-intersection property. Compatibility of q_n gives A-linearity of every augmentation comparison. All actions commute with S; no elementwise choice of different lifts at different cutoffs is substituted for a homomorphism.
hypotheses: A,R CNL_O(k) with finite residue; cofinal finite cutoffs; finite-level φ_n are local surjections.
End_S(M) carries the topology induced by evaluations on a finite generating set, equivalently its finite-module topology.
proofSteps: Define an endomorphism on compatible sections coordinatewise; transfer along PatchedModule.limitEquiv.
Multiplication, addition and O-scalars hold at every finite level, hence at the separated limit.
Lift φ_n via completeness and compare cofinal cutoffs with ideal powers; compactness supplies a single preimage for each r.
Continuity follows from locality and the finite-action cutoffs; generators test endomorphism convergence.
acceptance: Surjective φ_n do not imply surjectivity of φ_∞ for an arbitrary noncompact source.

nodes.title: Recovery of the original module
nodes.statement: Suppose the compatible datum maps give X_n/aX_n≃H/L_n H, with L_n cofinal open cutoffs for the finite complete module H, and their A-actions induced by φ_n. Then the induced map gives an A-linear equivalence M_∞/aM_∞≃H, where A acts on H through φ_∞. It agrees with all the original finite-level specialization maps and any retained finite list of comparisons. This theorem compares completed finite modules; it is not an unrestricted claim that inverse limits commute with quotienting.
hypotheses: a finitely generated; S and A Noetherian complete; finite M_∞ and H; L_n cofinal.
proofSteps: Identify (M_∞/aM_∞)/I_n with X_n/aX_n by right exactness of successive quotients.
The finite quotient M_∞/aM_∞ is complete; compare its reductions with H/L_n H.
Use the compatible actions and φ_∞ to prove A-linearity and compatibility with retained decorations.
acceptance: In the CG cutoffs, L_n=(π^n) and a=(z₁,…,z_q); a is not the ideal (π,z₁,…,z_q).

sources.locator: §2.2, Proposition 2.3 and proof, PDF pp. 11–14
sources.match: The patched augmentation quotient is the original H, including its action through φ_∞.

nodes.title: A compatible local power-series action
nodes.statement: Let S=O[[z₁,…,z_q]] and let the finite-level scalar image of S on X_n lie in the image of A. For the patched finite S-module M, compactness of A and closedness of the fibres imply image(S→End_O M)⊂image(A→End_O M). Thus M is finite over A. If the finite actions have fixed residue and are local on A/Ann_A M, there exists a continuous local O-algebra map iota:S→A with the same action on M. It is chosen by lifting the images of the finitely many variables to m_A and using R03.1 local series evaluation; the lift is generally not unique. If each finite augmentation action lies in the image of ker φ_n, then iota(a)⊂ker φ_∞+Ann_A M.
hypotheses: A compact CNL_O(k) ring; M finite S, nonzero for the local image-ring argument.
Augmentation containment is a separate hypothesis; it does not follow merely from scalar-image containment.
proofSteps: For each fixed s, compatible nonempty closed sets {a∈A : a and s have the same action on the first n reductions} give one common lift by compactness.
Any S-generating family then generates over A by image containment.
The quotient A/Ann M is complete local; the images of z_i lie in its maximal ideal. Lift them to m_A, evaluate power series, and compare actions on the separated limit.
To lift the augmentation kernel containment use the compact closed relation {(a,b): action(a)=action(z), φ_n(b)=0} at all cutoffs; quotient by Ann M gives the stated containment.
acceptance: Do not infer a canonical S→A or faithfulness from this construction.
For a zero module, finiteness is automatic; choose any local series map needed independently.

sources.locator: §2.2, Proposition 2.3 and proof, PDF pp. 11–14
sources.match: The scalar image is closed and the formal power-series variables can be lifted; finiteness and the augmentation ideal containment are separate outcomes.

nodes.title: Free-module patching
nodes.statement: Under the compatible decorated patching hypotheses, if each selected X_n is free of the same rank d over S/I_n and the retained based presentation has r=0, then M_∞≃S^d, with continuous A-action, a compatible local scalar lift S→A under the scalar-image hypothesis, finite generation over A, and augmentation specialization M_∞/aM_∞≃H. The theorem is integral. It does not assert M_∞ free over A or nearly faithful over A without numerical/component hypotheses.
hypotheses: Fixed rank and based free identifications must be retained in the finite decorations; no original-level transition maps required.
proofSteps: Apply extraction to the free bases together with actions and comparisons.
The limit relation map is zero, so the native quotient is S^d.
Apply patched action, scalar lift and augmentation specialization targets.
acceptance: At rank zero the output is zero and the later nonzero depth/support conclusions are unavailable.
At q=0, S=O and a=0, the output recovers H itself.

sources.locator: §4, proof of Theorem 4.1, printed pp. 218–221, PDF pp. 36–39
sources.match: The finite free framed modules patch to a finite free S_∞-module before the dimension and support argument.

nodes.title: Numerical depth bounds for patched modules
nodes.statement: Let S=O[[z₁,…,z_q]], of dimension q+1, and A a Noetherian local ring acting compatibly on a nonzero M finite over both rings through a local O-algebra map iota:S→A. Then depth_S M=depth_A M and dim_S M=dim_A M, where dimensions are support dimensions. (i) If M is S-free, depth_A M=q+1, so dim A≥q+1; if dim A≤q+1, equality holds and M is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over A. (ii) If M has a square S-presentation and dim_A M<q+1, the relation map is injective over the domain S by passing to its fraction field. For M≠0 its projective dimension is exactly 1 and depth_A M=q. If A is regular local of dimension q, the existing maximal-depth theorem makes M A-free. Full component support in case (i) is a separate R03.6 conclusion requiring its irreducibility hypotheses.
hypotheses: Finite-dimensional Noetherian local rings; M≠0; module finite over both rings; map S→A local.
Depth/dimension restriction-of-scalars is requested from R03.3; no equality for arbitrary infinite modules or nonlocal actions.
proofSteps: Use the requested finite-local-map depth and support-dimension comparison.
For S-free modules transfer the native regular parameter sequence (π,z₁,…,z_q), then use depth≤support dimension≤dim A.

For a square presentation tensor with Frac(S). Proper support dimension makes the cokernel vanish there, so the square matrix is bijective; its kernel is torsion-free as a submodule of S^d, hence zero.
M cannot be a nonzero free S-module with proper support, so AB gives projective dimension 1 and depth q; apply R03.3 maximal-depth freeness when A is regular.
acceptance: For S=k[[u,v]], the residue field is unbalanced and has projective dimension two; it is not covered by the square codimension-one case.
For A=O[[u,v]]/(uv), M=A/(u) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay supported only on one component; maximal depth does not supply full support.

sources.locator: §2.2, Proposition 2.3 and proof, PDF pp. 11–14
sources.match: The final proof passes from support dimension to an injective square relation map, then uses Auslander–Buchsbaum over both rings.

sources.locator: §4, proof of Theorem 4.1, printed pp. 218–221, PDF pp. 36–39
sources.match: The proof compares S-free depth with the separately computed deformation-ring dimension; irreducibility enters the support conclusion later.

nodes.title: The balanced-module patching theorem
nodes.statement: Let O be the integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p with p≥3, R∈CNL_O(k), and H a finite R-module finite over O. Let q≥1, A=O[[x₁,…,x_{q−1}]], S_N=O[(ℤ/p^Nℤ)^q]. For every N≥1 assume a continuous local surjection φ_N:A↠R and an A⊗_O S_N-module H_N such that: H_N is finite balanced over S_N; H_N/a_N^aug H_N≃H is A-linear through φ_N; image(S_N→End_O H_N)⊂image(A→End_O H_N); and image(a_N^aug→End_O H_N)⊂image(ker φ_N→End_O H_N). Then H is free over R. For H≠0 the patching constructs a nonzero A-free M_∞ and a local iota:S_∞→A, with ker φ_∞=iota(a)A, M_∞/aM_∞≃H and R≃A/iota(a)A. No complex patching theorem is an input.
hypotheses: The two image containments and the A-linearity of specialization are mandatory.
S_N is the group ring over O, not reduced modulo π; its residue field is k.
H=0 is permitted and handled before constructing the d_N cutoffs.
proofSteps: For H=0, H is free of rank zero. Otherwise d=dim_k(H/πH)>0.
Use balanced-square presentations and the cofinal b_N,d_N cutoffs to form D_{M,N}; d is constant by the augmentation identification and Nakayama.
Extract while preserving the action, φ, augmentation quotient and square based presentation.
Construct M_∞, φ_∞ and iota; M_∞ is finite over A. As dim A=q<dim S_∞=q+1, apply the numerical square-presentation target to obtain A-freeness.

A nonzero finite free module is faithful, so augmentation containment improves to iota(a)⊂ker φ_∞. The quotient M_∞/iota(a)M_∞ is nonzero free over A/iota(a)A and also has action through R; this forces ker φ_∞=iota(a)A.
The generalized support and kernel-descent API stays in R03.6; this final paragraph is the elementary quotient argument for this exact source theorem, not a duplicate general descent node.
acceptance: At q=1, A=O; a nonzero output is O-free before descent.
Balanced H_N are not assumed free over S_N.
The theorem gives integral freeness, stronger than the rational conclusion of Kisin’s criterion.

sources.locator: §2.2, Proposition 2.3 and proof, PDF pp. 11–14
sources.match: Retains the integrated target identifier and all hypotheses of Proposition 2.3, including the separate augmentation-kernel condition.

nodes.title: Ring and module patching data
nodes.statement: Fix the Kisin parameters: O with fraction field E and π, S=O[[y₁,…,y_{h+j}]], S₀=O[[y_{h+1},…,y_{h+j}]], B complete Noetherian local flat O-domain of dimension d+1, h+j≥d, C=B[[x₁,…,x_{h+j−d}]], and nonzero M of S₀-rank s. For m≥1 let c_m=(π^m,((1+y_i)^(p^m)−1)_{i≤h},(y_i^(p^m))_{i>h}). Write m_D^[r] for the ideal generated by rth powers of individual elements of m_D; it is not m_D^r. A ring-module datum at cutoff m and chosen positive bound r consists of S/c_m→D→R/(c_m R+m_R^[r]), C↠D, m_D^[r]=0, a D-module L free over S/c_m of rank s with a specified basis, and a C-linear surjection L↠M/c_m M. The ring maps and both module actions commute. Morphisms are C-algebra maps and compatible surjective module maps; equivalences preserve all maps and the chosen basis.
hypotheses: The S-action on R and M is induced by killing y₁,…,y_h; R is a B-algebra.
All rings D are complete local O-algebras with the fixed finite residue field.
The auxiliary bound r is positive; the h+j=0 case is handled directly rather than using a zero exponent cutoff.
proofSteps: Use native ring quotients, power-series rings, free coordinate modules, algebra maps and linear maps.
Retain the quotient ring as well as the action on L; it cannot be reconstructed merely from a potentially nonfaithful module action.
Fix the convention for element-power ideals explicitly before bounding finite quotients.
acceptance: The exponent r_m in the printed proof is s·m·p^m·(h+j); it is not s·m·p^(m(h+j)).

sources.locator: §3.3, Proposition 3.3.1 and proof, printed pp. 1157–1159, PDF pp. 75–77
sources.match: Uses the ring-module datum of the proof, including the element-power ideal and all algebra maps.

nodes.title: Simultaneous ring and free-module patching
nodes.statement: Assume the four finite-level conditions of the Kisin criterion stated below, with h+j>0. There exist compatible ring-module patch data and limits R_∞ and M_∞, a surjection C↠R_∞, maps S→R_∞↠R, and an R_∞-module M_∞ free of rank s>0 over S. With a=(y₁,…,y_h), R_∞/aR_∞≃R as B-algebras and M_∞/aM_∞≃M with their induced actions. Every map is continuous in the complete local topology. The cutoffs satisfy a uniform finite bound on the cardinality of D, independent of the large original level n≥m.
hypotheses: O and B in the stated complete Noetherian finite-residue setting; h+j>0; s=rank_{S₀}M>0.
For every n, R_n is a quotient of C and M_n is free over S/b_n with b_n⊂((1+y_i)^(p^n)−1)_{i≤h}.
proofSteps: M=M_n/aM_n is S₀-free of a constant positive rank because b_n⊂a; hence s is independent of n.

Use c_m as above and the printed r_m=s·m·p^m·(h+j). For a∈m_{R_n}, its action on M/(π,y_{h+1},…,y_{h+j})M is nilpotent on an s-dimensional vector space, so a^s M_n⊂(π,y₁,…,y_{h+j})M_n; modulo π, pigeonhole on the h+j variables shows a^(s·p^m·(h+j))M_n⊂(π,y_i^(p^m))_i M_n. Modulo c_m, the group relations give y_i^(p^m)∈(π) for i≤h, and the other powers vanish. Raising the resulting containment to the mth power gives a^(r_m)M_n⊂c_m M_n. This is an element-power calculation, not ordinary ideal-power nilpotence.

Set D_{m,n}=R_n/(c_m R_n+m_{R_n}^[r_m]) and L_{m,n}=M_n/c_m M_n. The ring has cardinality bounded by |C/m_C^[r_m]|; that quotient is finite because r_m>0 and the element-power ideal contains powers of a finite generating set of m_C.
Finite ring and based module decorations give a compatible subsequence by the same native finite-prefix compactness method; take native ring/module limits.

The fixed rank bases give S-freeness of M_∞. The retained maps C↠D_m lift to a surjection C↠R_∞ by compactness; the ring and module kernels after killing a are recovered by finite-quotient completeness.
acceptance: Record the additional ring-quotient kernel aR_∞; the module specialization by itself does not prove this kernel.
The printed h+j=0 cutoff has r_m=0 and is not used; that valid theorem boundary has a direct argument below.

sources.locator: §3.3, Proposition 3.3.1 and proof, printed pp. 1157–1159, PDF pp. 75–77
sources.match: Constructs the finite quotient rings D_{m,n}, patches them and the free modules, and recovers both specialization kernels.

nodes.title: Kisin’s module patching criterion
nodes.statement: Let O be the integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p with fraction field E. Let B be a complete Noetherian local flat O-algebra with fixed finite residue field, a domain of dimension d+1, with B[1/p] formally smooth over E in the source’s complete-local sense. Let R be a B-algebra, M≠0 an R-module, h,j≥0 and h+j≥d. For each n≥0 assume O-algebra maps S=O[[y₁,…,y_{h+j}]]→R_n↠R and an R_n-linear surjection M_n↠M with: the ring map B-linear; ker(R_n→R)=(y₁,…,y_h)R_n; ker(M_n→M)=(y₁,…,y_h)M_n; b_n=Ann_S M_n⊂((1+y_i)^(p^n)−1)_{i≤h}; M_n finite free over S/b_n; and R_n a B-algebra quotient of C=B[[x₁,…,x_{h+j−d}]]. Then R is finite over S₀=O[[y_{h+1},…,y_{h+j}]] and M⊗_O E is finite projective and faithful over R[1/p]. Integral projectivity, freeness or faithfulness is not asserted.
hypotheses: The source’s formal smoothness must provide regularity of C[1/p]; this interface is requested explicitly from R03.1 rather than silently replaced by algebraic Algebra.FormallySmooth.
The S₀-action is obtained by specialization and must be independent of n; all residue labels and local maps are as in §3.3.
proofSteps: For h+j>0 apply simultaneous ring-module patching. S and C are Noetherian domains of the same dimension h+j+1, M_∞≠0 is S-free and has the C-action.

Lift the images of the S-variables from R_∞ to m_C through C↠R_∞. R03.1 local series evaluation gives a local O-algebra map S→C whose composite is the existing S→R_∞, so the C-action on M_∞ restricts to its S-free action.

Import the same-dimensional-domain finiteness lemma (Kisin Lemma 3.3.4) already contained in the integrated R03.3 depth/dimension target: C is finite over S. Faithfulness of the S-free module makes S→C injective. After inverting p the finite injective map still gives equal dimensions; the requested regularity of S[1/p] and C[1/p] makes M_∞[1/p] finite projective faithful over C[1/p].
Faithfulness kills ker(C[1/p]→R_∞[1/p]); C is O-flat, so ker(C→R_∞)=0. Therefore C≃R_∞.

A nonzero finite projective faithful module has positive rank at every prime; this property survives the quotient by a. Descend projectivity and faithfulness only after inverting p. Ring finiteness over S survives quotienting to S₀.

For h+j=0, d=0 and h=j=0. The hypotheses give b_n=0, M_n=M free over O and R_n=R a quotient of B. Apply the same-dimensional-domain finiteness lemma directly with O→B and M≠0 to obtain B finite over O. The domain B[1/p] is then a field and the nonzero O-free M gives a faithful B[1/p]-action. Flatness of B kills ker(B→R), so R=B. The generic-fibre module is a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space, giving the stated rational projectivity/faithfulness without the zero-exponent patch cutoff.
acceptance: M≠0 is essential for the rank and faithfulness argument.
B domain and the dimension equality are essential; maximal depth alone does not make an arbitrary reducible action faithful.

sources.match: Retains the integrated criterion identifier and the exact separation between integral finiteness and generic-fibre projectivity/faithfulness.

nodes.title: Comparison of chosen patching constructions
nodes.statement: Two compatible towers with identical cutoff ideals and specified coherent equivalences preserving their presentations, actions, φ and augmentation maps induce a unique isomorphism of patched modules inducing those equivalences at every finite level. It intertwines the A-actions and specialization maps. Cofinal restriction is a special case. Unrelated diagonal subsequences need not have identical action-ring maps or canonically isomorphic patched modules, and no independence of such choices is claimed.
hypotheses: Actual coherent finite-level equivalences, not merely isomorphic underlying module types.
proofSteps: Apply the native limit universal property and transfer along PatchedModule.limitEquiv.
Check the inverse and all action/specialization identities by every finite projection.
Use cofinality only for a restriction of the already chosen tower.
acceptance: A different φ_N sequence may have the same H_N types but a different φ_∞; it is not identified by this theorem.

sources.locator: §2.2, Proposition 2.3 and proof, PDF pp. 11–14

nodes.title: Generic-fibre and integral conclusions differ
nodes.statement: For a complete DVR O, A=O[ε]/(πε,ε²) and M=A/(ε)≃O, M[1/π]≃A[1/π] is finite free faithful, whereas Ann_A M=(ε)≠0 integrally. Separately, for A=O[[u,v]]/(uv), M=A/(u), the sequence (π,v) is M-regular of length dim A=2, but M misses the component (v). These are diagnostic boundaries for the conclusions, not counterexamples to Kisin’s criterion, whose B is required flat and a domain.
hypotheses: O complete DVR with π≠0; use the native polynomial/power-series quotient rings and their actual modules.
proofSteps: In the first example π annihilates ε, so localization removes ε while its integral class remains nonzero.
In the second example M≃O[[v]] and π,v is regular; annihilator is (u), so its support is V(u), a proper component of Spec A.
Check this layer exports rational projective faithfulness only in Kisin’s case and maximal depth only before R03.6’s support hypotheses.
acceptance: Neither π-torsion in the action ring nor reducible component support may be silently erased from an integral assertion.

sources.match: The proposition states its projective and faithful conclusions only after inverting p; the example explains why this wording must survive translation.

sources.match: Near faithfulness follows only after the numerical bound and separate irreducibility/component hypotheses; the reducible example tests that boundary.

requests.need: Give the genuine residue-field module structure on native Tor₁^S(M,k), finite-dimensionality, and its identification with the residue of the first term of a minimal finite-free resolution. Relate β₀,β₁ to minimal generator and relation counts, including cancellation in any finite presentation. Keep ownership in the existing depth/homological layer, not in complex patching P8.

For a local homomorphism S→A of Noetherian local rings and a nonzero module finite over both, prove equality of depth and of support dimension under restriction of scalars, without requiring A finite over S. Use the finite image ring A/Ann_A M where necessary. Supply the regularity of S=O[[Fin q]], its dimension q+1, and the parameter regular sequence (π,z₁,…,z_q), connecting to native IsRegularLocalRing and Sequence.IsRegular.

Identify the complete-local formal smoothness used for B[1/p] in Kisin Proposition 3.3.1, and prove that it implies regularity of B[[Fin e]][1/p], with its actual completed local topology, for every finite e. Also supply regularity of O[[Fin q]][1/p]. Do not assert the algebraic Mathlib Algebra.FormallySmooth instance without a comparison theorem.

Check the mixed-characteristic element-power cutoff estimate in the Kisin construction when implementing it; the finite bound and zero-variable boundary are explicit.

gaps.title: Residue Tor and minimal-presentation interface
gaps.detail: The source calculation is read and its proof route fixed, but the existing supplier does not specify the residue-field lift of native Tor or the minimal-resolution comparison. Native Tor derives one factor and lacks this module-level API; the concrete square-presentation predicate is elaboratable while the canonical defect signatures remain omitted. The first R03.3 request must resolve this interface.

gaps.title: Depth and dimension comparison for a finite module over two local rings
gaps.detail: The integrated R03.3 target includes depth, AB and the same-dimension-domain lemma, but not this exact restriction-of-scalars statement or the finite-variable formal-series parameter calculation. CG uses both. The second R03.3 request records the precise module-finite hypotheses and should be supplied before claiming mathematical closure.

gaps.title: Kisin generic-fibre formal smoothness and regularity
gaps.detail: The paper uses complete-local generic-fibre formal smoothness to apply regularity after inversion. The R03.1 formal smoothness target is a small-extension lifting predicate for coefficient objects, not automatically an algebraic smoothness instance for B[1/p]. The precise comparison and regularity theorem is requested, so the suggested criterion does not encode an unspecified smoothness proposition.

sourceIssues.locator: Published Annals 170 (2009), §3.3, Proposition 3.3.1, definition of r_m and patching data, printed pp. 1157–1158, PDF pp. 75–76
sourceIssues.printed: The theorem permits h=j=d=0, but the uniform patching construction uses r_m=s·m·p^m·(h+j) and requires m_D^[r_m]=0 in a nonzero local ring.
sourceIssues.correction: Handle h+j=0 separately: M is a nonzero finite free O-module and R a quotient of the one-dimensional O-flat domain B. Lemma 3.3.4 gives B finite over O; B[1/p] is a field and acts faithfully on M[1/p]. O-flatness kills the kernel B→R, so R=B and the rational conclusion follows.
sourceIssues.reason: When h+j=0 the exponent is zero. The ideal generated by zeroth powers of maximal-ideal elements contains 1, so the constructed ring quotient is zero and cannot carry the required residue field. The stated theorem remains valid by the direct argument; its hypotheses need no restriction.
